redundancy_check.note: All final units were cross-checked. No pairs substantially evaluate the same content: K1 covers Q2 P&L drivers (including efficiency measures), K5 covers strategic developments (CEO/Straumur), and other units address distinct financial metrics (balance sheet, capital, liquidity, segments, 6M performance). Each material fact belongs to only one unit.

key_information_units.information: Profit before tax decreased to ISK 1,545 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 2,025 million in Q2 2025, a decline of ISK 480 million or 23.7%, primarily due to a 26.8% drop in net fee income to ISK 1,416 million and a ISK 112 million one-off cost from efficiency measures announced in June; these measures are expected to lower the annual cost base by ISK 300-400 million, partially offset by resilient net interest income growth of 1.7%.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Profit before tax ISK 1,545 m. compared to ISK 2,025 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 480 m. from previous year, or 23.7%. Net interest income ISK 3,013 m. compared to ISK 2,962 m. in Q2 2025 Increasing by ISK 51 m. from previous year or 1.7%. Net fee and commission income ISK 1,416 m. compared to ISK 1,935 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 519 m. from previous year or 26.8%. Administrative expenses ISK 2,947 m. compared to ISK 2,981 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 34 m. from previous year or 1.1% despite ISK 112 m. one-off restructuring charge. Efficiency measures... ISK 112 m. expensed... lowers the annual cost base by ISK 300-400 m.

key_information_units.information: Deposits surpassed ISK 200 billion for the first time, reaching ISK 201.2 billion at quarter-end, up 16.5% from year-end 2025, driven by retail deposits and public entities, while loans to customers grew to ISK 223.3 billion, up 7.6% from year-end 2025.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025. Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025.

key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio (CAR) stood at 23.0% at 30 June 2026, down from 26.8% at year-end 2025 primarily due to the ISK 10.2 billion special dividend payment in June, while maintaining a strong management buffer above regulatory requirements.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026, decreasing as special dividend was distributed in June. The bank continues to target a management buffer of 2% to 4% over current and anticipated CAR requirements.

key_information_units.information: Liquidity position remains strong with LCR at 276% (well above 100% requirement) and NSFR at 137%, supported by high-quality liquid assets of ISK 76.4 billion (81% Level 1 assets).
key_information_units.source_evidence: The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remains strong at 276%, well above the 100% regulatory requirement. NSFR stood at 137%. High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) amounted to ISK 76.4 bn., of which 81% were classified as Level 1 assets.

key_information_units.information: CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson requested to step down by year-end 2026, and the divestment of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf. is ongoing.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson to step down by year-end 2026. Sale of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf. in progress.

key_information_units.information: Segment performance highlights strong loan growth in Commercial Banking (+ISK 6 bn QoQ) and Investment Banking (+nearly 4% QoQ), while UK operations show record loan book levels and advancing asset sales.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Commercial Banking: deposits increasing by ISK 12 bn. during Q2 (+8% QoQ), loans increasing in total by ISK 6 bn. during the quarter (+3%). Investment Banking: loan book grew by nearly 4% quarter-on-quarter. UK: loan book reaching an all-time high, Harpa completing additional PE deal, UK largest PE asset sale process expected to close before year-end.

key_information_units.information: Six-month 2026 results show pre-tax profit from continuing operations increased by 23.0% YoY to ISK 3,354 million, driven by 6.8% YoY growth in net interest income and disciplined cost management.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Pre-tax profit from continuing operations increasing by 23.0% YoY to ISK 3,354 million in 6M 2026. Net interest income increased by 6.8% YoY. Administrative expenses amounted to ISK 5,961 m., a 1.8% decrease YoY.
